summary: The claim is supported. The implementation measures median subpixel contour chords perpendicular to an ordered, smoothed, endpoint-trimmed centerline through the filled instance mask. Coordinate ordering and units are consistent, insufficient samples remain unavailable, representative track width comes from the largest-area eligible observed plane, legacy EDT measurements remain explicitly labelled, and primary tables and reports use the chord-width field. Eleven focused synthetic and reporting tests passed in the validated virtual environment. This quantity establishes apparent segmented-mask width only; it does not establish a PSF-corrected, molecular-scale, or true three-dimensional nuclear diameter.

findings.title: Near-isotropic XY calibration is represented by one averaged scale
findings.impact: Leica X and Y voxel sizes differing by at most 2% are averaged, so physical widths can retain a small orientation-dependent scale error even though larger anisotropy fails closed. This does not materially undermine the tested rotation-stability criterion but bounds its physical interpretation.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:11246-11258 rejects X/Y differences above 2% and averages accepted X and Y scales.
tests/test_saturn_v571_body_width.py:58-73 tests raster-orientation stability with isotropic pixels.
findings.recommendation: Retain the current fail-closed threshold and document the possible residual scale error; use separate X/Y physical coordinates if future acquisitions require materially anisotropic lateral calibration.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as required by the review instructions.

Focused synthetic tests validate rectangles, a tapered polygon, insufficient samples, field propagation, and representative-plane selection; they do not exhaust every concave, branched, or highly self-approaching mask geometry.
The measurement is conditional on the filled U-Net mask and derived centerline. It does not independently validate segmentation boundaries or optical resolution.
The result does not establish chromatin diameter, molecular-scale nucleus width, PSF-corrected width, or anatomical three-dimensional volume.
recommended_follow_up: Continue recording segmentation-boundary, focus, annotation-thickness, and lateral-PSF sensitivity wherever body width is reported.
If materially anisotropic XY acquisitions are introduced, add synthetic physical-coordinate tests and replace the scalar XY calibration with axis-specific chord scaling.
Consider adding an explicit synthetic concave-mask case to document nearest-enclosing-intersection behavior.
